Uncertainty-aware prediction of asphalt pavement roughness using probabilistic machine learning
abstract: Accurate prediction of asphalt pavement deterioration is critical for data-driven infrastructure asset management. However, conventional data-driven models commonly provide deterministic estimates, offering limited insight into prediction confidence. This limitation restricts their application in risk-aware decision-making, where understanding the reliability of each prediction is essential. This study addresses this challenge by developing an uncertainty-aware framework for predicting pavement roughness using data from the Long-Term Pavement Performance program. A curated dataset of 1,246 test sections across 50 states in the United States was compiled, covering diverse climate regions, structural configurations, traffic loading, and surface characteristics. Probabilistic modeling approaches, including Bayesian neural networks and Gaussian process regression, were used to predict pavement roughness while generating prediction intervals. Deterministic approaches, including random forest, extreme gradient boosting, support vector regression, and artificial neural networks, were also developed under the same validation and optimization framework for benchmarking. All models were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation and optimized using a Bayesian optimization framework. The results showed that extreme gradient boosting achieved the highest point prediction accuracy, while Gaussian process regression and Bayesian neural networks provided competitive accuracy, with coefficients of determination of 0.9133 and 0.9226, respectively, along with explicit uncertainty estimates. Gaussian process regression also demonstrated a reliable uncertainty calibration, with empirical coverage of 95% prediction intervals ranging from 88.89% to 96.31% across climate regions. Initial roughness, rutting, and cracking were identified as the dominant predictors. Regional analyses further revealed generally lower prediction errors in non-freezing regions, and spatial analyses identified geographic variations in pavement deterioration.

Energy-efficient deep learning-based vibration monitoring on parallel ultra-low-power microcontrollers
abstract: Structural health monitoring (SHM) through vibration analysis is essential for ensuring safety, reliability, and minimized maintenance costs in sensor-connected environments. Realizing this at the extreme edge, directly on sensor nodes, requires advanced data analytics, ultra-energy-efficient hardware, and high-fidelity datasets. This paper addresses these challenges by developing an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based deep learning framework for vibration-based structural health monitoring tailored to resource-constrained devices. We present a benchmarking dataset for vibration SHM, encompassing nine abnormal conditions that capture narrowband structural anomalies. Leveraging this dataset, we design supervised and unsupervised deep-learning models, integrating a system identification (SysId) preprocessing stage to derive structurally informed features that enhance model input quality. This improves algorithmic results while boosting hardware performances. These models are deployed on a parallel ultra-low-power microcontroller with dedicated hardware acceleration. Our unsupervised anomaly detectors deliver 89.90 percent (%) accuracy, 4.1 percentage points higher than the state-of-the-art attention-based baseline, favoring recall and missed-detection reduction at the cost of a higher false-alarm rate while consuming 13 microjoules (µJ) in low-power mode and requiring 370 microseconds (µs) in high-performance mode. This marks one of the first experimental validations of unsupervised on-device vibration diagnostics. Supervised counterparts achieve 96.06 % binary and 91.5 % multiclass accuracy, rivaling Residual Network (ResNet) with 1 5 . 8 × fewer parameters, at less than 235 µJ and not more than 6.3 ms (ms) inference. Relative to existing edge implementations, our approach is one to three orders of magnitude more energy-efficient and two orders faster, unlocking AI-enabled autonomous, low-latency predictive maintenance for large-scale distributed infrastructure monitoring.

title: Multi-objective optimized signal decomposition with explainable and reliable hybrid models for multistep significant wave height forecasting in ocean wave energy applications
abstract: Accurate forecasting of significant wave height (Hs) is vital for marine safety, coastal engineering, and renewable energy production. This study presents an effective integrated model system to forecast Hs for two distinct sites in Australia, Gladstone and Palm Beach, over various time horizons from 30-min to 24-h ahead during the period of 2018 to 2022. In the first stage, a novel multi-objective Optuna is developed to optimize the decomposition parameters using two criteria of compactness, bandwidth, and peakedness of a signal's frequency spectrum. The proposed methodology is utilized for hyperparameter tuning of Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA) and De-mixing Multivariate Variational Mode Decomposition (D-MVMD) techniques. This enables an optimal data decomposition process by eliminating the need for manual parameter selection. In the second stage, an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) approach, SHAPley Additive Explanations (SHAP), is used to identify the most influential components and analyze their interactions. These optimized and interpretable decomposed signals are then used as inputs to standalone forecasting models, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), deep Random Vector Functional Link (RVFL), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). These optimized and interpretable decomposed signals are then used as inputs to the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), deep Random Vector Functional Link (RVFL), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models to forecast. In the final stage, a comprehensive Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) is employed to quantify uncertainties and perform reliability analysis. The SHAP-based feature selection reduced the input variables from 37 to 48 decomposed components to a single dominant predictor while maintaining nearly identical predictive accuracy across all forecast horizons, significantly lowering computational costs. Among the models, the SSA-RVFL demonstrated superior performance, with lower computational cost and the highest forecasting accuracy across all time horizons. This model achieved the highest Index of Agreement (IA: 0.81-1) and determination coefficient (R 2 : 0.49-0.98), and lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE: 0.04-0.33) across stations and horizons. In addition, the results confirm operational reliability exceeding 88% for forecasts up to 6 h ahead. Overall, the fully optimized SSA integrated with the SHAP-RVFL-MCS results provides a robust framework for enhancing decision-making in coastal hazard and wave energy planning.

abstract: This paper implements artificial intelligence for month-ahead renewable power forecasting by fusing synchronized solar and wind information from the Sakaka Solar Plant and Dumat Al-Jandal Wind Farm in Saudi Arabia. Ten hybrid deep-learning architectures are evaluated under a common temporal framework using mean absolute error, root mean squared error, mean absolute percentage error, coefficient of determination, training time, and computational carbon dioxide emissions. The convolutional neural network-long short-term memory model with attention achieves the highest predictive accuracy, with a mean absolute error of 80, a root mean squared error of 129, a mean absolute percentage error of 6.6%, and a coefficient of determination of 0.87. The Temporal Fusion Transformer provides the strongest accuracy-sustainability compromise under the 70:30 Sustainable Artificial Intelligence score, while the wavelet-convolutional neural network-gated recurrent unit model records the lowest training footprint at 768 grams of carbon dioxide equivalent. A 10,000-draw perturbation sensitivity analysis of the error and emission values confirms that the preferred deployment model is decision-dependent rather than universally dominant: the Temporal Fusion Transformer is most frequently top-ranked under the central weighting, whereas carbon-heavier or carbon-lighter alternatives become preferred as decision weights change. The contribution is therefore system-level: the framework integrates cross-resource data fusion, leakage-aware long-horizon evaluation, carbon-aware model selection, Pareto analysis, and explicit decision-robustness testing. Reported carbon reductions refer to model computation and should not be interpreted as measured reductions in grid curtailment or citywide operational emissions.

A lightweight deep learning architecture for crack segmentation in structural health monitoring
abstract: Automated crack segmentation is a key component of vision-based structural health monitoring for civil infrastructure. However, many deep learning approaches remain computationally demanding for embedded edge devices and exhibit limited generalisation across diverse materials and imaging conditions. This paper presents a lightweight deep learning architecture designed to balance segmentation accuracy, computational efficiency, and cross-domain robustness. The artificial intelligence contribution is an efficient encoder–decoder integrating depthwise separable convolutions, lightweight multi-scale context aggregation, and channel attention. The proposed approach targets crack continuity through a unified design for thin-structure segmentation under strict computational constraints. The engineering contribution is a practical inspection method for structural health monitoring systems with limited memory, latency, and power budgets. Experiments on a joint dataset comprising 30,017 crack images collected from 20 heterogeneous datasets demonstrate competitive performance across diverse conditions. The proposed Lightweight Attention Channel-Enhanced Crack Segmentation (LACE-Crack) architecture achieves a higher harmonic mean of precision and recall (F1 score) (0.569 vs. 0.566), precision (0.751 vs. 0.732), mean intersection over union (0.694 vs. 0.693), optimal image scale (0.489 vs. 0.480), and optimal dataset scale (0.425 vs. 0.411) than the comparison architecture, with comparable recall (0.459 vs. 0.462). It also requires approximately 43% fewer parameters and 64% fewer floating-point operations. These results demonstrate a strong balance between crack segmentation performance and computational efficiency, supporting the practical use of lightweight artificial intelligence for infrastructure inspection under deployment constraints.

title: A multi-stage graph-conditioned probabilistic forecaster with dual-stream temporal encoding for wind speed forecasting
abstract: Accurate wind speed forecasting is a critical foundation for wind power dispatch and the grid integration of renewable energy. The non-stationary fluctuations in wind speed time series, the spatially dependent variations among multiple wind turbines, and forecasting uncertainties continue to pose significant challenges for wind farm-level forecasting. This paper proposes an artificial intelligence framework for multi-turbine wind speed forecasting, termed the Multi-Stage Graph-Conditioned Probabilistic Forecaster (MGPF).The model fuses prior graphs and data-driven graphs at the node-pair level, enabling differentiated spatial connection representations for different wind turbine pairs. Simultaneously, it sets up two candidate temporal encoding paths, a Generative Pre-trained Transformer 2 (GPT-2) and a lightweight Patch, and determines the appropriate configuration based on comparative results across different datasets. Spatio-temporal cross-attention further establishes interactions between spatial and temporal features, while the probabilistic prediction head constructs prediction intervals by estimating the mean and variance of future wind speeds. Experimental results on two wind farm datasets with markedly different scales show that MGPF reduces the root mean square error (RMSE) by 35.56% and 3.92%, respectively, compared to the corresponding optimal baselines, experiments at the Kelmarsh external wind farm further validate the model's applicability under different wind farm data conditions. Probabilistic forecast results show that MGPF outperforms the probabilistic baseline overall in terms of probability distribution fitting and forecast interval quality, encoder and pre-training control experiments also validate the effectiveness of the time-encoding design.

title: A condition-aware adaptive physics-informed residual network for chiller energy consumption modeling
Structured variational quantum control for spin-chain state transfer: Expressivity, trainability, and robustness
abstract: We propose a hybrid variational framework for quantum optimal control of high-fidelity state transfer in spin chains. The continuous-time control problem is reformulated as a trainable Trotterized quantum circuit, where drift dynamics are encoded by fixed two-qubit interaction blocks and control fields by parameterized on-site R Z rotations. This provides a physics-informed variational ansatz directly connecting the Hamiltonian model to hybrid quantum–classical optimization. We compare two control parameterizations: an expressive local scheme with site-wise trainable parameters and a compact global scheme with shared parameters per Trotter layer. Numerical experiments on XXZ spin chains show that both achieve near-unit fidelity for the main noiseless end-to-end transfer task. The reduced optimization dimension of the global parameterization provides favorable optimization behavior for several larger systems, while additional source–target experiments demonstrate that this advantage is task dependent and that local control can perform better for interior transfers. Studies under depolarizing and dephasing noise show that relative noise-induced degradation depends on system size, noise strength, and noise model, with no uniform robustness ordering. Additional analyses examine circuit depth, initialization sensitivity, empirical gradient statistics, interaction anisotropy, Trotter error, exact piecewise-constant control, and hardware execution. Overall, the results reveal a trade-off between control expressivity, optimization dimensionality, task structure, and noise sensitivity, providing a physically grounded framework for structured variational quantum control of distributed quantum systems.

title: Uncertainty-aware surrogate-assisted optimization for concrete mix design using data-centric and physics-informed learning
